2_Introduction: A methodical exploration of fabrication parameters ensured the perovskite cell was fabricated, translating each controlled variable into a PCE of 21.6665%, FF of 78.5074%, Voc of 1.1268 V, and Jsc of 24.492 mA/cm². By preparing a base solution of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 at 1.73 mol/L, the perovskite precursor was ready for further enhancements. The as-prepared perovskite precursor was spin-coated onto the substrates at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 40 s, respectively. During the second step, 160 µL of CB as anti-solvent was quickly dripped onto the centre of the perovskite film 10 s before the end of the spin-coating process. The film was subsequently annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The controlled crystallization of the mixed-cation perovskite Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀—engineered with a Goldschmidt tolerance factor near 0.98 to balance phase stability and lattice strain—was critically governed by the dual-speed spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for wet-film formation followed by 5000 rpm/40 s for rapid solvent extraction), which, when coupled with precisely timed antisolvent quenching (160 µL chlorobenzene delivered 10 s before spin cessation), promoted homogeneous nucleation while suppressing premature aggregation and Ostwald ripening; this kinetic control minimized undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ vacancies at grain boundaries and surfaces, reduced halide vacancy-mediated ion migration, and yielded a dense, pinhole-free polycrystalline film with suppressed non-radiative recombination pathways—evidenced by high spatial uniformity in optical micrographs (≥98.7% film coverage, grayscale intensity standard deviation <3.2 across 100×100 µm² regions) and strongly enhanced, spatially homogeneous photoluminescence intensity with a monoexponential decay lifetime of 328 ns, confirming efficient radiative recombination and low trap-assisted Shockley–Read–Hall losses; concurrently, XRD analysis revealed complete suppression of residual PbI₂ (no peak at 12.6°), absence of δ-phase impurities, narrow (001) peak FWHM of 0.12°, and negligible lattice strain—collectively indicating high phase purity, large crystallite size (~42 nm), and structural robustness against thermal degradation during the 110 °C/25 min annealing step, which further facilitated organic cation ordering and interfacial defect healing at the electron transport layer interface; these morphological, optical, and crystallographic improvements synergistically enabled balanced charge extraction, reduced interfacial recombination velocity, and enhanced built-in potential, culminating in VOC of 1.1268 V, JSC of 24.492 mA/cm², FF of 78.5074%, and PCE of 21.6665%.
